LESSON: GRAMMAR IN USE 9.3.1 ADVERBS

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 9
Topic 9.3: Grammar in Use 9.3.1 Adverbs

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Grammar in Use 9.3.1 Adverbs. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How do we show where, how, when and how many times an action occurs?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify adverbs in oral and written texts
2. use adverbs to express different meanings correctly

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE LEARNING: GRAMMAR IN USE 9.3.1 ADVERBS
This lesson teaches Grammar in Use 9.3.1 Adverbs for Grade 6 ENGLISH LANGUAGE.

STUDY STEPS
1. identify adverbs in oral and written texts
   Practise this until you can do it without help.
2. use adverbs to express different meanings correctly
   Practise this until you can do it without help.

HOW TO SHOW UNDERSTANDING
Explain the idea in your own words, give one Kenyan example, then complete the practice tasks.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Describe Grammar in Use 9.3.1 Adverbs using something at your school.

Example 2: Give a home/community example from your county.

Example 3: Teach a younger child one idea from this lesson in simple words.

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Underline the key ideas about Grammar in Use 9.3.1 Adverbs above.
2. Explain Grammar in Use 9.3.1 Adverbs to a parent using one local example.
3. Write or draw three things that prove you understand Grammar in Use 9.3.1 Adverbs.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Grammar in Use 9.3.1 Adverbs with school or home examples.
2. Answer: Why is Grammar in Use 9.3.1 Adverbs important for a Grade 6 learner?
3. Prepare a one-minute oral presentation for a parent or teacher.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How do we show where, how, when and how many times an action occurs?
2. What are some of the words you could use to talk more about an action?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. identify adverbs in oral and written texts
2. use adverbs to express different meanings correctly

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
